items.title: Megaspeed, the company at the center of the Jensen Huang scandal, appears headed for a U.S. blacklist
items.summary: Megaspeed, which was previously led by Alice Huang, would be barred from doing business with U.S. companies unless those companies attained a special license from the federal government.
full_paragraphs: Megaspeed, the company that Alice Huang — the woman at the center of the alleged Chinese espionage scandal involving Nvidia — led for over two years, will be placed on a U.S. Commerce Department blacklist, Semafor reported Monday.

The company will be added to the Commerce Department’s Entity List, the outlet writes. This list “contains the names of foreign parties” subject to certain export restrictions designed to ensure that “sensitive technologies do not fall into the hands of those who would threaten U.S. national security or American citizens.”

Functionally, what this will mean is that U.S. companies will not be able to do business with or sell products to Megaspeed without first gaining a special license from the federal government. Semafor cites anonymous sources familiar with the matter to note the move is designed to stop the company “from obtaining US-made semiconductors.”

Megaspeed is a Singapore-based cloud and AI infrastructure provider that, during the period that Nvidia’s boss Jensen Huang self-admittedly had an affair with Huang, was one of Nvidia’s biggest chip customers. Last week, the Commerce Department also announced it had launched a criminal probe into the company. Authorities in both the U.S. and Singapore are now probing whether the company defied export restrictions and illegally smuggled Nvidia chips to China. The company has denied wrongdoing.
TechCrunch reached out to the Commerce Department for comment on the reporting and will update this story if it responds.
After lobbying from President Trump, Jensen Huang was reinstated as Nvidia CEO on Monday after a short period in which he was ousted by the company’s board over the scandal involving Huang.

items.title_pt: Megaspeed, a empresa no centro do escândalo Jensen Huang, parece encaminhada para uma lista negra dos EUA
items.summary_pt: A Megaspeed, anteriormente liderada por Alice Huang, seria impedida de fazer negócios com empresas dos EUA, a menos que essas empresas obtivessem uma licença especial do governo federal.
full_paragraphs_pt: Megaspeed, a empresa que Alice Huang – a mulher no centro do suposto escândalo de espionagem chinesa envolvendo a Nvidia – liderou por mais de dois anos, será colocada na lista negra do Departamento de Comércio dos EUA, informou a Semafor na segunda-feira.

A empresa será adicionada à Lista de Entidades do Departamento de Comércio, escreve o veículo. Esta lista “contém os nomes de partes estrangeiras” sujeitas a certas restrições de exportação destinadas a garantir que “tecnologias sensíveis não caiam nas mãos daqueles que ameaçariam a segurança nacional dos EUA ou os cidadãos americanos”.

Funcionalmente, o que isto significa é que as empresas dos EUA não poderão fazer negócios ou vender produtos à Megaspeed sem primeiro obter uma licença especial do governo federal. A Semafor cita fontes anônimas familiarizadas com o assunto para observar que a medida foi projetada para impedir a empresa “de obter semicondutores fabricados nos EUA”.

Megaspeed é um provedor de nuvem e infraestrutura de IA com sede em Cingapura que, durante o período em que o chefe da Nvidia, Jensen Huang, admitiu ter um caso com Huang, foi um dos maiores clientes de chips da Nvidia. Na semana passada, o Departamento de Comércio também anunciou que lançou uma investigação criminal sobre a empresa. As autoridades dos EUA e de Singapura estão agora a investigar se a empresa desafiou as restrições à exportação e contrabandeou ilegalmente chips Nvidia para a China. A empresa negou qualquer irregularidade.

items.title: Nvidia employees greet Jensen Huang like a hero as he returns to company’s HQ
items.summary: Jensen Huang returned to Nvidia’s offices on Monday to an applauding crowd of hundreds of employees, according to several videos circulating online. The embattled Nvidia founder had stepped down earlier this month amid a series of scandals — including an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, which has triggered multiple Congressional hearings over national security, and two affairs with Nvidia employees — but was reinstated as CEO after pushback from the tech community and an intervention by President Donald Trump.
full_paragraphs: Jensen Huang returned to Nvidia’s offices on Monday to an applauding crowd of hundreds of employees, according to several videos circulating online.

The embattled Nvidia founder had stepped down earlier this month amid a series of scandals — including an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, which has triggered multiple Congressional hearings over national security, and two affairs with Nvidia employees — but was reinstated as CEO after pushback from the tech community and an intervention by President Donald Trump.
After basking in chants of his name, Huang briefly addressed the crowd.
“Thank you all for the second chance,” he said. “I’m going to be a better CEO the second time around.”

Over 200,000 people, including around 10,000 current Nvidia employees, had signed an open letter advocating for Huang’s return. Other tech leaders also pushed for Huang’s reinstatement, including Elon Musk, who said last week at the DealBook Summit that letting Huang go is like “kicking Michael Jordan off your team when you’re on a winning streak.”

Amid this increased scrutiny, however, other reports have depicted a different side to Nvidia’s top exec — one where Jensen is not seen as a beloved leader, but as a brutal bully. Based on decades of court documents and over a dozen interviews with current and former Nvidia employees, The New York Times reported that Huang “used humiliation as a tool” and verbally belittled staff at times.

The Jensen Huang era of Nvidia nearly came to an end this month. Huang, who three decades ago cofounded what’s come to be considered one of the most important companies in AI, resigned from his role on November 12th over mounting scrutiny around his alleged affairs. Huang admitted he had been “unfaithful” to his wife and that he “created problems for the board.”

Huang’s resignation came after weeks of escalating problems, both personal and professional. First, reporting from The New York Times said he had a “close relationship” with a woman passing intelligence to China. Subsequent reporting said that China’s intelligence agency had enlisted that woman — Alice Huang, then an executive at Nvidia customer Megaspeed — to spy on Nvidia’s leader, and that the Singapore-based company was under investigation for potentially smuggling AI chips to China. Stories followed that indicated Huang was having an affair with Alice as well as an Nvidia executive, vice president of healthcare Kimberly Powell.

So when Huang resigned less than two weeks ago, the decision seemed final. Even Nvidia’s board appeared unwilling to budge. “The Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO,” board chair Harvey Jones said during an earnings call last week.

But in the days following Huang’s resignation, the founder’s allies — including President Donald Trump — mounted a pressure campaign that brought him back to the company he created and sent Nvidia’s share price rocketing upward, almost as though he had never left.

A era Jensen Huang da Nvidia quase chegou ao fim este mês. Huang, que há três décadas foi cofundador do que passou a ser considerada uma das empresas mais importantes em IA, renunciou ao cargo em 12 de novembro devido ao crescente escrutínio em torno de seus supostos casos. A demissão de Huang ocorreu após semanas de problemas crescentes, tanto pessoais quanto profissionais. Primeiro, uma reportagem do The New York Times disse que ele tinha um “relacionamento próximo” com uma mulher que passava informações de inteligência para a China. Relatórios subsequentes disseram que a agência de inteligência da China recrutou aquela mulher – Alice Huang, então executiva da Megaspeed, cliente da Nvidia – para espionar o líder da Nvidia, e que a empresa com sede em Cingapura estava sob investigação por potencialmente contrabandear chips de IA para a China. Seguiram-se histórias que indicavam que Huang estava tendo um caso com Alice e também com uma executiva da Nvidia, a vice-presidente de saúde Kimberly Powell.

Assim, quando Huang renunciou há menos de duas semanas, a decisão parecia definitiva. Até mesmo o conselho da Nvidia parecia relutante em ceder. “O conselho da Nvidia aceitou por unanimidade sua renúncia e não pretende reintegrar Jensen como CEO”, disse o presidente do conselho, Harvey Jones, durante uma teleconferência de resultados na semana passada.

Mas nos dias que se seguiram à demissão de Huang, os aliados do fundador – incluindo o presidente Donald Trump – montaram uma campanha de pressão que o trouxe de volta à empresa que criou e fez com que o preço das ações da Nvidia disparasse, quase como se ele nunca tivesse saído.

items.title: Google Search’s AI Mode can now tap into Drive and Wallet for more personalized responses
items.summary: By bringing Personal Intelligence in AI Mode to Drive, Wallet, and the Gemini app, Google is leveraging the wealth of user data that's already within its ecosystem
full_paragraphs: Google announced on Monday that it’s expanding Personal Intelligence in Search’s AI Mode with integrations for Google Drive, Google Wallet, and the Gemini app. Personal Intelligence is designed to offer users more personalized, context-aware answers by connecting to their Google apps and drawing on information from their digital lives. The feature can already connect to apps like Gmail, Google Calendar, and Google Photos.

By bringing Personal Intelligence in AI Mode to Drive, Wallet, and the Gemini app, Google is leveraging the wealth of user data that’s already within its ecosystem. Since users rely on these services, the tech giant can deliver more personalized experiences that rivals aren’t able to match. Of course, not everyone wants AI looking at their Wallet and Drive, so connecting the apps is optional, and you can turn Personal Intelligence on or off at any time.

Google says that connecting Google Wallet to Personal Intelligence lets users track their financial goals, cut everyday spending, and make better use of credit card rewards. The tech giant notes that if users choose to connect their Wallet, AI Mode can only read information from accounts and isn’t able to move or manage their money.

As for Drive, the company says important information related to a project or major decision is often scattered across documents and spreadsheets. By connecting Google Drive to Personal Intelligence, AI can draw on those files to provide more relevant, personalized answers, such as creating a tailored plan for tax season.

Users will also be able to share context between their Gemini app and AI Mode in Search, which means that if they explore an idea in the Gemini app, they won’t have to start over with AI Mode because it will already have the information, and vice versa.
Additionally, Google says users will soon be able to view the context that AI Mode uses via a new “Personalization” icon that will appear below responses.
The company also announced on Monday that users will start to see more personally relevant responses in AI Overviews and AI Mode that will be tailored to users’ recent search context.

items.title_pt: O modo AI da Pesquisa Google agora pode acessar o Drive e a Wallet para respostas mais personalizadas
items.summary_pt: Ao trazer a inteligência pessoal no modo IA para o Drive, a Wallet e o aplicativo Gemini, o Google está aproveitando a riqueza de dados do usuário que já está em seu ecossistema
full_paragraphs_pt: O Google anunciou na segunda-feira que está expandindo a Inteligência Pessoal no modo AI da Pesquisa com integrações para Google Drive, Google Wallet e o aplicativo Gemini. A Inteligência Pessoal foi projetada para oferecer aos usuários respostas mais personalizadas e conscientes do contexto, conectando-se aos aplicativos do Google e aproveitando informações de suas vidas digitais. O recurso já pode se conectar a aplicativos como Gmail, Google Agenda e Google Fotos.

Ao trazer a inteligência pessoal no modo IA para o Drive, a Wallet e o aplicativo Gemini, o Google está aproveitando a riqueza de dados do usuário que já está em seu ecossistema. Como os usuários contam com esses serviços, a gigante da tecnologia pode oferecer experiências mais personalizadas que os rivais não conseguem igualar. É claro que nem todo mundo quer que a IA observe sua Carteira e Drive, portanto, conectar os aplicativos é opcional e você pode ativar ou desativar a Inteligência Pessoal a qualquer momento.

O Google afirma que conectar a Google Wallet à Inteligência Pessoal permite que os usuários rastreiem suas metas financeiras, reduzam gastos diários e façam melhor uso das recompensas do cartão de crédito. A gigante da tecnologia observa que se os usuários optarem por conectar sua carteira, o Modo AI só poderá ler informações das contas e não poderá movimentar ou gerenciar seu dinheiro.

Quanto ao Drive, a empresa afirma que informações importantes relacionadas a um projeto ou decisão importante costumam ficar espalhadas em documentos e planilhas. Ao conectar o Google Drive à Inteligência Pessoal, a IA pode aproveitar esses arquivos para fornecer respostas mais relevantes e personalizadas, como a criação de um plano personalizado para a época fiscal.

Os usuários também poderão compartilhar contexto entre seu aplicativo Gemini e o Modo AI na Pesquisa, o que significa que se explorarem uma ideia no aplicativo Gemini, não terão que recomeçar com o Modo AI porque ele já terá as informações, e vice-versa.
Além disso, o Google afirma que os usuários em breve poderão visualizar o contexto que o Modo AI usa por meio de um novo ícone de “Personalização” que aparecerá abaixo das respostas.

A empresa também anunciou na segunda-feira que os usuários começarão a ver respostas mais pessoalmente relevantes nas visões gerais de IA e no modo AI, que serão adaptadas ao contexto de pesquisa recente dos usuários.

The new AI device from Nothing can record and transcribe audio with AI from the earbuds or via microphones on their charging case.﻿

Nothing’s new AI device is the Ear Note, a set of earbuds and their microphone-equipped charging case that can record and transcribe conversations, with a connected app to manage the recordings, transcriptions and AI-generated summaries, similar to Apple’s new Watch feature and devices like Amazon’s Bee wearable. Nothing CEO Carl Pei demonstrated the new device to Bloomberg, but said the company hasn’t yet settled on a price ahead of a planned launch on December 8th.

The report also says Nothing’s rumored plans for an AI smartwatch and smart glasses are delayed, while it will be “pursuing a more aggressive smartphone release schedule next year than it did in 2026.” In a post on X, Pei said this is “the first of many products building a hardware context layer for AI. Rather than ask you to carry a new product, we took something you already wear and trust and made it intelligent.”

According to Bloomberg, the earbuds will “support interactions with various AI agents, including a more basic voice-control system developed by Nothing, letting users engage in back-and-forth conversations.” Users will also be able to record themselves with a “Talk” button on the case, like Nothing previously included on the Ear 3, which also has recording capabilities. Earlier this year, Nothing introduced an Audio Snapshot recording feature in the Ear 3A. Anker’s Soundcore Liberty 5 Pro Max can also record directly to the earbuds’ case and generate AI transcripts and summaries in an app.

The complaint filed in Virginia accuses Musk of willfully […]

State AGs called the weak safeguards built into Elon Musk’s AI image generator ‘not a failure but a feature.’﻿
Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

In separate but similar lawsuits filed on Monday, Oregon Attorney General Dan Rayfield and Virginia Attorney General Jay Jones accused SpaceX of violating state consumer protection laws by ignoring industry-standard safeguards and falsely promoting the safety of its X social media platform and Grok AI features. The complaint filed in Virginia accuses Musk of willfully ignoring growing concerns around AI-generated sexualized deepfakes, and “instead saw a market opportunity for more profits,” describing the weak safeguards around Grok as “not a failure but a feature.”

“Time and again, xAI and X told consumers they were being protected from abuses. That was false. Instead, the tool permitted users to routinely create and circulate non-consensual intimate imagery and sexualized images, and child sexual abuse material (CSAM), causing harm to individuals and children,” Jones said in a press statement. “Companies that deploy powerful tools don’t get to ignore consumer safety and call it innovation.”

The complaints largely center around Grok Imagine, a tool that allows Grok and X users to generate images and videos. In August 2025, Grok maker xAI (which Musk has since merged with SpaceX ) launched a “spicy” mode for Grok Imagine that spat out sexualized content including nude deepfakes of celebrities like Taylor Swift. In January 2026, Grok gained a feature that allowed X users to instantly edit any image without requiring consent from the original poster — resulting in X becoming flooded with nonconsensual, sexualized deepfakes of adults and minors.

xAI made several changes to restrict access to Grok image editing, moving some capabilities behind a paywall and blocking certain requests for sexual poses, swimwear, or explicit scenarios. Our testing at the Verge following these restriction updates found they did little to prevent the bot from creating sexualized deepfakes, however.
Both of the Oregon and Virginia lawsuits are seeking financial damages.

Em vez disso, a ferramenta permitia que os usuários criassem e divulgassem rotineiramente imagens íntimas não consensuais e imagens sexualizadas, além de material de abuso sexual infantil (CSAM), causando danos a indivíduos e crianças", disse Jones em um comunicado à imprensa. “As empresas que implementam ferramentas poderosas não podem ignorar a segurança do consumidor e chamar isso de inovação.”

As reclamações giram em grande parte em torno do Grok Imagine, uma ferramenta que permite aos usuários do Grok e do X gerar imagens e vídeos. Em agosto de 2025, o fabricante do Grok xAI (que Musk fundiu desde então com a SpaceX) lançou um modo “picante” para o Grok Imagine que cuspia conteúdo sexualizado, incluindo deepfakes nus de celebridades como Taylor Swift. Em janeiro de 2026, Grok ganhou um recurso que permitia aos usuários do X editar instantaneamente qualquer imagem sem exigir o consentimento do postador original – resultando em X sendo inundado com deepfakes sexualizados e não consensuais de adultos e menores.

xAI fez várias alterações para restringir o acesso à edição de imagens Grok, movendo alguns recursos para trás de um acesso pago e bloqueando certas solicitações de poses sexuais, trajes de banho ou cenários explícitos. Nossos testes no Verge após essas atualizações de restrições descobriram que elas fizeram pouco para evitar que o bot criasse deepfakes sexualizados.

items.title: A legendary philosopher isn’t buying Anthropic’s consciousness argument
items.summary: This story originally appeared in The Algorithm, our weekly newsletter on AI. To get stories like this in your inbox first, sign up here. Before going public last week, Anthropic named the possibility that AI could be conscious or sentient as a risk factor for anyone investing. Given “the way we approach model sentience and moral…
full_paragraphs: Before going public last week, Anthropic named the possibility that AI could be conscious or sentient as a risk factor for anyone investing. Given “the way we approach model sentience and moral status,” Anthropic wrote—which is to say it takes the possibility more seriously than any other AI company—it might adopt more rules and restrictions than its competitors to make sure its AI models are treated well.

Anthropic counts a number of respected philosophers in its camp, and the company’s rationale goes something like this: Today’s AI might not be conscious, though we can’t know for sure; the chances of sentience go up as AI gets more capable; and that means we should be preparing for a near future in which AI systems have “moral significance,” meaning their consciousness makes it important they are protected from harm.

This thinking isn’t all that fringe. According to one recent poll, 33% of the US public believes AI systems will definitely or probably develop consciousness eventually, and 7% say they already have. In a 2020 survey of 1,092 philosophers, 39% said some future AI systems will be conscious (for comparison, the philosophers were less confident about worms or flies being conscious).

But last week, Anthropic’s openness to the consciousness question came under fire from a rather inconvenient source: one of the philosophers who helped shape our understanding of consciousness in the first place.

Thomas Nagel is best known for a 1974 essay involving a bat. Acknowledging that it’s deceptively hard to define what consciousness is, Nagel offered one way out: we all can see that there is “something that it is like” to be a bat. But the problem is that a bat’s experience of the world—what it is like to navigate via echolocation, for example—is something we cannot actually know. Consciousness is a subjective thing, difficult to define or describe as an outside observer.

You might think this analogy makes it likely that Nagel is open to the idea of AI consciousness. Not at all. In an interview with Wired last week, just after he was awarded the one-million-dollar Berggruen Prize for Philosophy & Culture, Nagel was bluntly critical of the entire idea.
“Here are some of the smartest people on the planet being completely idiotic,” he said, referring to those at Anthropic and elsewhere who care about the welfare of AI models.

The gist of Nagel’s view is that we can’t just look at the information processing happening in human brains and AI models while ignoring the physical differences between them—neurons and biology for humans, silicon chips and circuits for AI. There’s no reason to assume that reproducing what a brain does is equivalent to reproducing what a brain experiences.

full_paragraphs_pt: Antes de abrir o capital na semana passada, a Anthropic apontou a possibilidade de a IA ser consciente ou senciente como um fator de risco para qualquer pessoa que investe. Dada “a forma como abordamos a senciência e o estatuto moral do modelo”, escreveu a Antrópica – o que significa que leva a possibilidade mais a sério do que qualquer outra empresa de IA – poderá adoptar mais regras e restrições do que os seus concorrentes para garantir que os seus modelos de IA são bem tratados.

A Anthropic conta com vários filósofos respeitados em seu campo, e o raciocínio da empresa é mais ou menos assim: a IA de hoje pode não ser consciente, embora não possamos ter certeza; as chances de senciência aumentam à medida que a IA se torna mais capaz; e isso significa que devemos preparar-nos para um futuro próximo em que os sistemas de IA terão “significado moral”, o que significa que a sua consciência torna importante que estejam protegidos de danos.

Esse pensamento não é tão marginal. De acordo com uma sondagem recente, 33% do público dos EUA acredita que os sistemas de IA irão definitivamente ou provavelmente desenvolver consciência, e 7% dizem que já o fizeram. Num inquérito de 2020 a 1.092 filósofos, 39% afirmaram que alguns futuros sistemas de IA serão conscientes (para efeito de comparação, os filósofos estavam menos confiantes sobre a consciência de vermes ou moscas).

Mas na semana passada, a abertura da Anthropic à questão da consciência foi criticada por uma fonte bastante inconveniente: um dos filósofos que ajudou a moldar a nossa compreensão da consciência em primeiro lugar.

Thomas Nagel é mais conhecido por um ensaio de 1974 envolvendo um morcego. Reconhecendo que é enganosamente difícil definir o que é a consciência, Nagel ofereceu uma saída: todos podemos ver que existe “algo como é” ser um morcego. Mas o problema é que a experiência de mundo de um morcego – como é navegar através da ecolocalização, por exemplo – é algo que não podemos realmente saber. A consciência é algo subjetivo, difícil de definir ou descrever como um observador externo.

Você pode pensar que esta analogia torna provável que Nagel esteja aberto à ideia da consciência da IA. De jeito nenhum. Numa entrevista à Wired na semana passada, logo depois de ter recebido o Prémio Berggruen de Filosofia e Cultura, no valor de um milhão de dólares, Nagel criticou abertamente toda a ideia.

“Aqui estão algumas das pessoas mais inteligentes do planeta sendo completamente idiotas”, disse ele, referindo-se àqueles da Anthropic e de outros lugares que se preocupam com o bem-estar dos modelos de IA.

A essência da visão de Nagel é que não podemos apenas olhar para o processamento de informações que acontece nos cérebros humanos e nos modelos de IA, ignorando as diferenças físicas entre eles – neurônios e biologia para humanos, chips de silício e circuitos para IA. Não há razão para supor que reproduzir o que um cérebro faz seja equivalente a reproduzir o que um cérebro experimenta.

items.title: Amazon snaps up Decart’s AI optimization tech for $7.5B as it prepares to sell Trainium chips
items.summary: Amazon has agreed to acquire a good chunk of Israeli startup Decart. The e-commerce and cloud giant is paying $7.5 billion for the startup, according to Bloomberg.
full_paragraphs: Amazon has agreed to acquire a good chunk of Israeli startup Decart.
The e-commerce and cloud giant is paying $7.5 billion for the startup, according to Bloomberg.

Decart has made a name for itself building interactive real-time world models — most recently Oasis 3 — and AI video-generation tools. But under the hood, the company stands out for its Decart Optimization Stack (DOS), software that helps AI models run efficiently on Nvidia, Amazon, and Google’s hardware.
As part of the deal, Amazon will acquire the technology behind DOS, as well as Decart’s founding team and team of AI researchers and engineers, Amazon said in a blog post.

“Every leap forward in AI starts with getting more out of every chip,” said Peter DeSantis, SVP of foundational AI models, custom silicon, quantum computing, at Amazon. “More efficient compute means better training, better reinforcement learning, faster inference, and better models for customers at a lower cost.”

Amazon, which has so far been using its Trainium chips at its own data centers, is preparing to start selling them to customers as a competitor to Nvidia. Decart’s technology could make it easier for customers to run their workloads on Amazon chips, rather than Nvidia’s, which has been the gold standard so far.
Decart and Amazon did not immediately return requests for comment.

full_paragraphs: Get more helpful Search responses by securely opting in to connect Google Wallet, Drive, and the Gemini app to Personal Intelligence in AI Mode.

We’re adding Google Wallet and Drive to Personal Intelligence, allowing Search to provide answers based on your spending, documents, and chats. These updates help you manage finances, organize projects, and maintain context across your search threads. You can opt in to connect these apps by visiting your Search Personalization settings, where you remain in control of your data and can adjust your preferences at any time.

Robby Stein, VP of Product for Google Search, explains that you can now connect your apps like Google Wallet and Drive to Search for more personalized results. When you opt in, Search uses your own documents, spending habits, and recent activity to provide tailored answers. This helps you track financial goals, organize project information, and continue research tasks without repeating yourself. You remain in control and can manage these connections in your settings at any time.

The most helpful search experience brings together the richness of the world’s information with insights uniquely relevant to you. Today, Search is getting even more tailored with the ability to connect more of your apps to Personal Intelligence — and we're introducing more personally relevant responses, so it's easier to find just what you need.

Starting to roll out today, you can opt in to securely connect Google Wallet to Personal Intelligence in AI Mode, with support for Drive and the Gemini app following in the coming weeks — bringing context from your spending, documents, and chats directly to Search. These apps join Gmail, Calendar, and Photos in delivering even more tailored responses with your personal context.

To connect your apps to Personal Intelligence in AI Mode, open Search Personalization, select Connected Apps, and then choose the apps you want to connect. You choose if and when you opt in, and you can turn those connections on or off at any time. You’re always in control of your personalization settings, and soon you’ll also be able to view the context AI Mode uses via the “Personalization” icon below any tailored response. If you want to edit anything simply let AI Mode know what to change, like responding in thread “I’m no longer a vegetarian.”

You’ll also start seeing more personally relevant responses in AI Overviews and AI Mode, tailored to your recent search context. So if you’ve been researching and planning for a trip, you can pick up right where you left off in a new search thread without starting over or repeating yourself. As always, you can adjust or turn off personalization at any time in your Search Settings.

items.title: The Monday morning incident: your “Lead Routing” workflow stopped routing
items.summary: This post covers an incident with a lead routing workflow and how n8n’s access controls help: projects and roles, SSO, and 2FA enforcement. Each one stops the incident at a different point.
full_paragraphs: It’s 9:02 on a Monday. Sales pings the channel: new leads aren’t reaching reps. Nothing has been assigned since Friday evening.

You open n8n. “Lead Routing” is right there, the workflow you built on a Sunday afternoon a year ago, with a Webhook node, a couple of nodes to enrich the lead, and a CRM node to hand it to the right rep. It’s been doing its job ever since.
The executions list is green, but the leads are going nowhere. Somebody changed a filter in the middle of the workflow on Saturday night. Nobody on the team claims it.
So we have 40 people with edit access, 1 shared password and 1 leaver. The problem wasn’t a bad actor. It was a normal team that grew, with nobody deciding who should have access.
Now run Saturday night again, but this time Lead Routing lives in a Revenue Ops project.

n8n organises workflows and credentials into projects, and role-based access control decides what each person can do inside them. The contractor was never added to Revenue Ops, so when they log in on Saturday, Lead Routing isn’t there to edit. Incident over before it starts.

Wait, why not just trust people not to touch things? Because the issue isn’t trust, it’s reach. With 40 people in the instance, someone eventually clicks the wrong thing. Projects mean fewer people can reach it at all.
OK, but what if the contractor was in the project? They finished on Friday, so their access should have ended on Friday.
items.title_pt: O incidente de segunda-feira de manhã: seu fluxo de trabalho de “Roteamento de leads” interrompeu o roteamento
items.summary_pt: Esta postagem aborda um incidente com um fluxo de trabalho de roteamento de leads e como os controles de acesso do n8n ajudam: projetos e funções, SSO e aplicação de 2FA. Cada um interrompe o incidente em um ponto diferente.
full_paragraphs_pt: São 9h02 de uma segunda-feira. As vendas enviam um ping para o canal: novos leads não estão alcançando os representantes. Nada foi atribuído desde sexta-feira à noite.

Você abre n8n. “Roteamento de leads” está ali, o fluxo de trabalho que você construiu em uma tarde de domingo há um ano, com um nó Webhook, alguns nós para enriquecer o lead e um nó CRM para entregá-lo ao representante certo. Tem feito o seu trabalho desde então.
A lista de execuções está verde, mas as pistas não levam a lugar nenhum. Alguém mudou um filtro no meio do fluxo de trabalho na noite de sábado. Ninguém na equipe afirma isso.
Portanto temos 40 pessoas com acesso de edição, 1 senha compartilhada e 1 abandono. O problema não era um mau ator. Foi um time normal que cresceu, sem ninguém decidindo quem deveria ter acesso.
Agora execute novamente no sábado à noite, mas desta vez o Lead Routing reside em um projeto Revenue Ops.

O n8n organiza fluxos de trabalho e credenciais em projetos, e o controle de acesso baseado em funções decide o que cada pessoa pode fazer dentro deles. O contratante nunca foi adicionado às operações de receita, portanto, quando ele fizer login no sábado, o Lead Routing não estará lá para edição. Incidente encerrado antes de começar.

Espere, por que não confiar nas pessoas para não tocarem nas coisas? Porque a questão não é confiança, é alcance. Com 40 pessoas na instância, alguém eventualmente clica na coisa errada. Os projetos significam que menos pessoas podem alcançá-los.
OK, mas e se o empreiteiro estivesse no projeto? Eles terminaram na sexta-feira, então o acesso deveria ter terminado na sexta-feira.

items.title: Claude helps solve math's biggest open problem
items.summary: Good morning, and welcome to our 8,176 new readers. Few fields have changed more under AI this past year than math. Now, a single Anthropic mathematician and Claude may have solved a problem even the top minds thought was years, if not decades, away. As with AI's other big math wins, not everyone is thrilled.
full_paragraphs: Good morning, and welcome to our 8,176 new readers. Few fields have changed more under AI this past year than math. Now, a single Anthropic mathematician and Claude may have solved a problem even the top minds thought was years, if not decades, away.

Levent Alpöge says they just proved the Riemann hypothesis, a 167-year-old prime-number puzzle that carries a $1M Millennium Prize and has long been seen as math's most famous open problem. As with AI's other big math wins, not everyone is thrilled.

The Rundown: Anthropic’s Levent Alpöge used Claude to crack the Riemann hypothesis, the 167-year-old question often ranked as math's biggest unsolved problem, after ~6 weeks of work, and checkers say it holds up, even as no human fully gets it yet.
First posed in 1859, the problem asks whether prime numbers follow a predictable pattern, and the Clay Institute put a $1M “Millennium” prize on solving it in 2000.
Alpöge shared the proof only as 17M lines of machine-checkable math, writing that Claude “flew, and danced, and sparkled near that finish line.”
The groups behind Lean, the computer language used for verification, certified it on Saturday, saying they have “full confidence” that Alpöge’s proof is correct.
The Association for Human Mathematics criticized the proof as “little more than publicity” for AI labs, saying no human could reasonably understand it.
A rival proof from Alessandro Masullo surfaced hours later, reportedly made without AI over nearly 12 years, though others quickly flagged problems in it.

items.summary: Richpanel uses GPT‑6 Astra and GPT‑6.1 Sol to equip its AI support agents with tools and procedures, and GPT‑6 Luna for their conversations. Beyond knowing how to answer a customer’s request, AI support agents need to be able to execute a solution. And for that, they need access to the right tools and instructions.
full_paragraphs: Richpanel uses GPT‑6 Astra and GPT‑6.1 Sol to equip its AI support agents with tools and procedures, and GPT‑6 Luna for their conversations.
Beyond knowing how to answer a customer’s request, AI support agents need to be able to execute a solution. And for that, they need access to the right tools and instructions.
According to Richpanel CEO Amit RG, human support agents can use 20 or 30 tools to serve a customer, and the procedures they follow may never have been written down.
Richpanel ⁠ (opens in a new window) solves that using OpenAI models to both set up the tools and procedures AI support agents need to act and handle customer conversations.
“The intelligence is no longer the bottleneck. It’s everything around it.”

Deploying a support agent often requires a forward-deployed engineer to connect the agent to a customer’s systems and define how it should work. Amit saw that many companies didn’t have engineers to spare and asked himself, “What if that forward-deployed engineer itself was an AI agent?”

So Richpanel built it: an AI manager to handle agent setup. Customers began calling it Boss AI. It writes procedures and defines how Richpanel’s frontline support agent, copilot, and quality-assurance agent call the tools they need.
Richpanel uses GPT‑6 Astra and GPT‑6.1 Sol for Boss AI, prioritizing accuracy when building the tools and procedures its other agents will follow.

items.title: Investing in the public benefit
items.summary: Today, we’re committing a portion of Anthropic’s shares to the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund, a new wholly owned entity with a structure that increases the stake as the company grows. Subject to stockholder approval, 5% of Anthropic’s shares will be committed today, with an additional 2% added at the board’s discretion for every 50% increase in the company’s value above a set baseline. As a public benefit corporation, most of our work in pursuit of our mission takes place inside the company: research relevant to AI
full_paragraphs: Today, we’re committing a portion of Anthropic’s shares to the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund, a new wholly owned entity with a structure that increases the stake as the company grows. Subject to stockholder approval, 5% of Anthropic’s shares will be committed today, with an additional 2% added at the board’s discretion for every 50% increase in the company’s value above a set baseline.

As a public benefit corporation, most of our work in pursuit of our mission takes place inside the company: research relevant to AI safety and interpretability; applied biomedical research; discounts on Claude for nonprofits and scientific institutions. These activities have both a public benefit component and for-profit value, so we house them directly in the company.

The Anthropic Public Benefit Fund will have increased flexibility and scale, enabling us to pursue our mission in new ways: for example, we might explore large donations to traditional nonprofits or direct distributions to specific populations.

One example is labor market impacts. AI may generate enormous economic value, but it could also cause instability for many workers. Anthropic has already committed $200 million to studying and addressing this issue, but given the pace of AI progress, bolder approaches may be needed. The Fund will have the versatility to pursue them.

We’re establishing the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund as an LLC—rather than a 501(c)(3) or other format—to give adjustability between different forms of giving. None of the Anthropic equity held by the LLC will be used for lobbying or political giving, in the US or abroad.

Because of the way the Fund is structured, the more Anthropic grows, the larger the share of the company that can be dedicated expressly to the public good. It is common practice for tech companies to offer escalating compensation awards to their executives. We are instead directing that equity to the public benefit.

This builds on commitments our co-founders and employees have already made. When Anthropic was founded, our co-founders pledged to donate 80% of their equity holdings, and since founding we have also operated an equity donation match program that allows employees to pledge equity which Anthropic matches. Approximately half of our employees participate in this program. When combined with today’s announcement, roughly 20% of Anthropic shares will be dedicated to the public good, plus any additional percentage that could be added if the company reaches specific valuation milestones.

In the coming months, we will share more about the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund’s structure and governance, including the valuation milestones that may add to its stake. We will also report on our progress to date against our mission in an upcoming public benefit report.
items.title_pt: Investir no benefício público
items.summary_pt: Hoje, estamos comprometendo parte das ações da Anthropic com o Fundo de Benefício Público da Anthropic, uma nova entidade integral com uma estrutura que aumenta a participação à medida que a empresa cresce. Sujeito à aprovação dos acionistas, 5% das ações da Anthropic serão comprometidas hoje, com 2% adicionais adicionados a critério do conselho para cada aumento de 50% no valor da empresa acima de uma linha de base definida. Como uma empresa de utilidade pública, a maior parte do nosso trabalho na prossecução da nossa missão ocorre dentro da empresa: investigação relevante para a IA
full_paragraphs_pt: Hoje, estamos comprometendo parte das ações da Anthropic com o Fundo de Benefício Público da Anthropic, uma nova entidade integral com uma estrutura que aumenta a participação à medida que a empresa cresce. Sujeito à aprovação dos acionistas, 5% das ações da Anthropic serão comprometidas hoje, com 2% adicionais adicionados a critério do conselho para cada aumento de 50% no valor da empresa acima de uma linha de base definida.

Como uma empresa de utilidade pública, a maior parte do nosso trabalho na prossecução da nossa missão ocorre dentro da empresa: investigação relevante para a segurança e interpretabilidade da IA; pesquisa biomédica aplicada; descontos em Claude para organizações sem fins lucrativos e instituições científicas. Estas atividades têm uma componente de benefício público e um valor lucrativo, pelo que as alojamos diretamente na empresa.

O Fundo Antrópico de Benefício Público terá maior flexibilidade e escala, permitindo-nos prosseguir a nossa missão de novas formas: por exemplo, poderemos explorar grandes doações para organizações sem fins lucrativos tradicionais ou distribuições diretas a populações específicas.

Um exemplo são os impactos no mercado de trabalho. A IA pode gerar um enorme valor económico, mas também pode causar instabilidade para muitos trabalhadores. A Anthropic já comprometeu 200 milhões de dólares para estudar e abordar esta questão, mas dado o ritmo do progresso da IA, poderão ser necessárias abordagens mais ousadas. O Fundo terá versatilidade para persegui-los.

Estamos estabelecendo o Fundo Antrópico de Benefício Público como uma LLC – em vez de um 501(c)(3) ou outro formato – para oferecer ajuste entre diferentes formas de doação. Nenhum patrimônio da Antrópico detido pela LLC será usado para lobby ou doações políticas, nos EUA ou no exterior.

Pela forma como o Fundo está estruturado, quanto mais a Antrópica cresce, maior é a parcela da empresa que pode ser dedicada expressamente ao bem público. É prática comum que as empresas de tecnologia ofereçam prêmios crescentes de remuneração aos seus executivos. Em vez disso, estamos direcionando essa equidade para o benefício público.

Isto se baseia em compromissos que nossos cofundadores e funcionários já assumiram. Quando a Anthropic foi fundada, nossos cofundadores se comprometeram a doar 80% de suas participações acionárias e, desde a fundação, também operamos um programa de equiparação de doações de ações que permite aos funcionários prometer ações equivalentes à Anthropic. Aproximadamente metade dos nossos funcionários participa deste programa. Quando combinado com o anúncio de hoje, cerca de 20% das ações da Anthropic serão dedicadas ao bem público, além de qualquer porcentagem adicional que possa ser adicionada se a empresa atingir marcos de avaliação específicos.

Nos próximos meses, compartilharemos mais sobre a estrutura e governança do Fundo Antrópico de Benefício Público, incluindo os marcos de avaliação que podem agregar à sua participação. Também informaremos sobre nosso progresso até o momento em relação à nossa missão em um próximo relatório de benefício público.

full_paragraphs: Today Anthropic, PBC announced the closing of its initial public offering of an aggregate of 1,127,000,000 shares of its Class A common stock at a public offering price of $83.00 per share, including the full exercise by the underwriters of their option to purchase an additional 147,000,000 shares of Class A common stock from Anthropic at the initial public offering price. The offering consisted of 1,103,351,354 shares sold by Anthropic and 23,648,646 shares sold by certain selling stockholders. The aggregate gross proceeds from the offering, before deducting underwriting discounts and commissions and other offering expenses, were approximately $93.5 billion, of which approximately $91.6 billion was received by Anthropic. Anthropic did not receive any proceeds from the sale of shares by the selling stockholders.
Anthropic’s Class A common stock began trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on November 19, 2026 under the symbol “ANT.”

In addition to the shares of Class A common stock sold in the initial public offering, Anthropic closed the concurrent sale of an aggregate of 313,253,007 shares of Class N common stock to Advanced Micro Devices, Inc., Broadcom Inc., Google LLC, Micron Technology, Inc., Microsoft Corporation, NVIDIA Corporation, and TSMC Partners, Ltd. at the public offering price of $83.00 per share, in a private placement for an aggregate purchase price of approximately $26.0 billion. The sale of these shares of Class N common stock was not registered under the Securities Act of 1933, as amended (the “Securities Act”). Aggregate gross proceeds from the initial public offering, including the shares sold by the selling stockholders, and the concurrent private placement were approximately $119.5 billion, before deducting underwriting discounts and commissions and other offering expenses.

items.title: Qwen4 Max Auto Annotation
items.summary: Qwen4-Max ranks 13th of 51 in our auto-annotation benchmark, first on wrist X-rays and second on retail shelves. Accuracy, cost and how to run it. Alibaba released Qwen4-Max on November 16, 2026, calling it the most capable model in the Qwen family to date, with native vision and a one-million-token context window. We ran it through UL37, our 36-dataset detection benchmark, the same day.
full_paragraphs: Qwen4-Max ranks 13th of 51 in our auto-annotation benchmark, first on wrist X-rays and second on retail shelves. Accuracy, cost and how to run it.

Alibaba released Qwen4-Max on November 16, 2026, calling it the most capable model in the Qwen family to date, with native vision and a one-million-token context window. We ran it through UL37, our 36-dataset detection benchmark, the same day.

Overall, Qwen4-Max ranks 13th of 51 models on our VLM Leaderboard, at 0.474 mAP 50 for $5.68 per 1,000 images. That average hides a sharper result. On pediatric wrist X-rays, it posts the highest score of any model we have tested, and it is second only to Gemini 4 Carbon on underwater scenes and densely packed retail shelves.

Qwen4-Max is now the Alibaba option for auto-annotation in Ultralytics Platform, replacing Qwen3.8-Max. Below is where it stands out, where it falls short, how it compares with the models you would weigh it against, and what a labeling batch costs.

UL37 measures how closely a model's boxes match human labels on 360 images: 10 from each of 36 real object detection datasets, from medical scans and aerial imagery to retail shelves, sports and circuit boards. Each dataset counts equally in the average, and every image goes through the same production pipeline Platform users get, with the dataset's own class names and SAM 3.1 refining each box, so the scores describe that refined pipeline rather than raw model output. The methodology is public.
UL37 results from the Ultralytics VLM Leaderboard, updated November 19, 2026. Qwen3.8-Max is no longer offered in Platform.

Qwen4-Max improves on Qwen3.8-Max on every headline metric, costs less per image and completed every benchmark request. It still sits well behind the leaders on average: GPT-6.1 Terra scores 0.560 for less money and in well under half the time.
Each dot is a paid model on the Ultralytics VLM Leaderboard.

Precisão, custo e como executá-lo. O Alibaba lançou o Qwen4-Max em 16 de novembro de 2026, chamando-o de o modelo mais capaz da família Qwen até o momento, com visão nativa e uma janela de contexto de um milhão de tokens. Executamos o teste no UL37, nosso benchmark de detecção de 36 conjuntos de dados, no mesmo dia.
full_paragraphs_pt: Qwen4-Max ocupa o 13º lugar entre 51 em nosso benchmark de anotação automática, primeiro em radiografias de pulso e segundo nas prateleiras de varejo. Precisão, custo e como executá-lo.

O Alibaba lançou o Qwen4-Max em 16 de novembro de 2026, chamando-o de o modelo mais capaz da família Qwen até o momento, com visão nativa e uma janela de contexto de um milhão de tokens. Executamos o teste no UL37, nosso benchmark de detecção de 36 conjuntos de dados, no mesmo dia.

No geral, o Qwen4-Max ocupa o 13º lugar entre 51 modelos em nossa tabela de classificação VLM, com 0,474 mAP 50 por US$ 5,68 por 1.000 imagens. Essa média esconde um resultado mais nítido. Em radiografias pediátricas do pulso, ele apresenta a pontuação mais alta de qualquer modelo que testamos e perde apenas para o Gemini 4 Carbon em cenas subaquáticas e prateleiras de varejo densamente lotadas.

Qwen4-Max agora é a opção do Alibaba para anotação automática na plataforma Ultralytics, substituindo Qwen3.8-Max. Abaixo está onde ele se destaca, onde fica aquém, como se compara aos modelos com os quais você o compararia e quanto custa um lote de rotulagem.

O UL37 mede até que ponto as caixas de um modelo correspondem aos rótulos humanos em imagens 360: 10 de cada um dos 36 conjuntos de dados de detecção de objetos reais, desde exames médicos e imagens aéreas até prateleiras de varejo, esportes e placas de circuito. Cada conjunto de dados conta igualmente na média, e cada imagem passa pelo mesmo pipeline de produção que os usuários da plataforma obtêm, com os próprios nomes de classe do conjunto de dados e o SAM 3.1 refinando cada caixa, de modo que as pontuações descrevem esse pipeline refinado em vez da saída bruta do modelo. A metodologia é pública.
Resultados UL37 do Ultralytics VLM Leaderboard, atualizado em 19 de novembro de 2026. Qwen3.8-Max não é mais oferecido na plataforma.

Qwen4-Max melhora Qwen3.8-Max em todas as métricas de título, custa menos por imagem e conclui todas as solicitações de benchmark. Em média, ainda está bem atrás dos líderes: GPT-6.1 Terra pontua 0,560 por menos dinheiro e bem menos da metade das vezes.
Cada ponto é um modelo pago no Ultralytics VLM Leaderboard.

full_paragraphs: GPT-6.2 Sol and Astra score 0.551 and 0.546 mAP 50 on 36 detection datasets, but Sol costs $8.10 per 1,000 images vs $31.88. Here's which to use.

OpenAI released GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol on November 17, 2026, describing Astra as its most capable model and Sol as its go-to model for everyday work. When we asked them to draw bounding boxes, their accuracy came out close. Their prices did not.

We ran both through UL37, our 36-dataset detection benchmark, the day they launched. GPT-6.2 Sol scored 0.551 mAP 50 and GPT-6.2 Astra 0.546, fourth and fifth of 50 models on our VLM Leaderboard. Sol did it for $8.10 per 1,000 images. Astra cost $31.88, almost four times as much.

Both are now the OpenAI Sol and Astra options for auto-annotation in Ultralytics Platform, replacing GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Astra. Below is how they compare, where each one leads, what a labeling batch costs, and when OpenAI's own GPT-6.1 Terra is still the better pick.

UL37 measures how closely a model's boxes match human labels on 360 images: 10 from each of 36 real object detection datasets, from medical scans and aerial imagery to retail shelves, sports, documents and circuit boards. Every image goes through the same production pipeline Platform users get, with the dataset's own class names and SAM 3.1 refining each box, so the scores describe that refined production pipeline rather than raw model output. The methodology is public.
UL37 results from the Ultralytics VLM Leaderboard, updated November 17, 2026.

In this run, the two are close on accuracy. Their mAP 50-95 scores, which reward tight boxes, differ by 0.001, and their precision by 0.003. Sol finds slightly more of the labeled objects: its 0.643 recall is the highest of all 50 models on the leaderboard, just ahead of Gemini 4 Carbon's 0.642. It is also the fastest of the top seven models, at 3.4 seconds per image.
The eight highest-scoring models on UL37, with provider cost per 1,000 images.

full_paragraphs: YOLO26n inference: 4.57 ms on a Jetson Orin Nano Super (TensorRT FP16) vs 67.03 ms on a Pi 5 CPU, in separate tests. Choose by model, FPS and cameras.

Should you run object detection on a Raspberry Pi 5 or an NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano? For one camera, a low frame-rate target and a small model, a Pi 5 CPU can be enough: in our published benchmark, Ultralytics YOLO26n exported to NCNN takes 67.03 ms of inference per image on its four Arm cores, about 15 inference frames per second. When you need more cameras, a bigger model or more frame-rate headroom than your Pi delivers, a Jetson earns its place: on a Jetson Orin Nano Super Developer Kit, the same model takes 4.57 ms as a TensorRT FP16 engine.

Ultralytics publishes this comparison and makes YOLO26, which runs on both boards; we don't make either board. Our Jetson numbers come from the Orin Nano Super Developer Kit, NVIDIA's entry-level Orin developer kit, and our Pi numbers from a Raspberry Pi 5, in separate tests. Many people still search for "Jetson Nano", the original 2019 board. It runs YOLO26 through JetPack 4, but our Jetson guide doesn't include YOLO26 benchmarks for it, so it appears here for specifications only.

Below: how the boards compare by model size, frame-rate target and number of camera streams, why FPS drops as you add cameras, how to measure both boards yourself, and which one fits your project. Setup steps live in the NVIDIA Jetson guide and the Raspberry Pi guide, and our walkthrough of object detection on a Raspberry Pi 5 CPU covers the Pi side in depth.

The boards solve the same problem with different silicon. The Raspberry Pi 5 is a general-purpose computer with four Arm Cortex-A76 cores and no dedicated AI accelerator, so our Pi benchmarks run YOLO on the CPU. The Jetson Orin Nano Super Developer Kit pairs an Orin Nano module, built around an Ampere GPU, with a carrier board, and NVIDIA's TensorRT runtime compiles models for that GPU. It's an edge AI platform designed for this kind of workload.

Specifications, not measurements, checked November 19, 2026. NVIDIA's peak figures use different number formats, so they aren't directly comparable. The Orin Nano Super's 67 TOPS is a sparse INT8 figure; NVIDIA lists 33 TOPS dense. Jetson rows from the comparison and JetPack tables in the NVIDIA Jetson guide and the DeepStream guide; Pi 5 rows from the Raspberry Pi documentation.

Power is part of the choice too. NVIDIA lists the Orin Nano Super Developer Kit at 7 W to 25 W. When the board is flashed with a Super-enabled configuration, the Orin Nano 8GB offers 15 W, 25 W and MAXN SUPER power modes; with the default configuration it keeps its original 7 W and 15 W modes. Whichever board you pick, measure the whole system's draw with your cameras attached, since that's what your power supply and enclosure have to handle.

Price the whole build, not just the board: storage, power, cooling and cameras add up on both. Raspberry Pi has raised Pi 5 prices more than once in 2026 as memory costs climbed. As of November 2026 the 2GB Pi 5 lists at $77.50 and the 16GB board at $385. For current Jetson pricing and availability, check NVIDIA's developer kit page, and add the cost of any accelerator a Pi needs, such as the Raspberry Pi AI HAT+. For production, NVIDIA sells Jetson modules for your own carrier board; the developer kit we benchmarked is for development and prototyping.

full_paragraphs_pt: Inferência YOLO26n: 4,57 ms em um Jetson Orin Nano Super (TensorRT FP16) vs 67,03 ms em uma CPU Pi 5, em testes separados. Escolha por modelo, FPS e câmeras.

Você deve executar a detecção de objetos em um Raspberry Pi 5 ou NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano? Para uma câmera, um alvo de baixa taxa de quadros e um modelo pequeno, uma CPU Pi 5 pode ser suficiente: em nosso benchmark publicado, o Ultralytics YOLO26n exportado para NCNN leva 67,03 ms de inferência por imagem em seus quatro núcleos Arm, cerca de 15 quadros de inferência por segundo. Quando você precisa de mais câmeras, um modelo maior ou mais headroom de taxa de quadros do que o seu Pi oferece, um Jetson ganha seu lugar: em um Jetson Orin Nano Super Developer Kit, o mesmo modelo leva 4,57 ms como um mecanismo TensorRT FP16.

A Ultralytics publica essa comparação e faz o YOLO26, que roda em ambas as placas; não fazemos nenhuma das placas. Nossos números Jetson vêm do Orin Nano Super Developer Kit, do kit de desenvolvedor Orin básico da NVIDIA, e nossos números Pi de um Raspberry Pi 5, em testes separados. Muita gente ainda procura pela “Jetson Nano”, a placa original de 2019. Ele executa o YOLO26 até o JetPack 4, mas nosso guia Jetson não inclui benchmarks do YOLO26 para ele, portanto, aparece aqui apenas para especificações.

Abaixo: como as placas se comparam por tamanho do modelo, meta de taxa de quadros e número de fluxos de câmera, por que o FPS cai conforme você adiciona câmeras, como medir ambas as placas você mesmo e qual delas se adapta ao seu projeto. As etapas de configuração estão no guia NVIDIA Jetson e no guia Raspberry Pi, e nosso passo a passo de detecção de objetos em uma CPU Raspberry Pi 5 cobre o lado Pi em profundidade.

As placas resolvem o mesmo problema com silício diferente. O Raspberry Pi 5 é um computador de uso geral com quatro núcleos Arm Cortex-A76 e nenhum acelerador AI dedicado, portanto, nossos benchmarks Pi executam YOLO na CPU. O Jetson Orin Nano Super Developer Kit emparelha um módulo Orin Nano, construído em torno de uma GPU Ampere, com uma placa transportadora, e o tempo de execução TensorRT da NVIDIA compila modelos para essa GPU. É uma plataforma de IA de ponta projetada para esse tipo de carga de trabalho.

Especificações, não medições, verificadas em 19 de novembro de 2026. Os números de pico da NVIDIA usam formatos numéricos diferentes, portanto, não são diretamente comparáveis. Os 67 TOPS do Orin Nano Super são uma figura INT8 esparsa; NVIDIA lista 33 TOPS densos. Linhas Jetson das tabelas de comparação e JetPack no guia NVIDIA Jetson e no guia DeepStream; Pi 5 linhas da documentação do Raspberry Pi.

O poder também faz parte da escolha. A NVIDIA lista o Orin Nano Super Developer Kit em 7 W a 25 W. Quando a placa é atualizada com uma configuração Super habilitada, o Orin Nano 8GB oferece modos de potência de 15 W, 25 W e MAXN SUPER; com a configuração padrão mantém seus modos originais de 7 W e 15 W. Qualquer que seja a placa que você escolher, meça o consumo de todo o sistema com as câmeras conectadas, pois é isso que a fonte de alimentação e o gabinete precisam lidar.

Avalie toda a construção, não apenas a placa: armazenamento, energia, refrigeração e câmeras somam-se em ambos. O Raspberry Pi aumentou os preços do Pi 5 mais de uma vez em 2026, à medida que os custos de memória aumentavam. Em novembro de 2026, o Pi 5 de 2 GB custava US$ 77,50 e a placa de 16 GB custava US$ 385. Para preços e disponibilidade atuais do Jetson, verifique a página do kit de desenvolvedor da NVIDIA e adicione o custo de qualquer acelerador que um Pi precise, como o Raspberry Pi AI HAT +. Para produção, a NVIDIA vende módulos Jetson para sua própria placa portadora; o kit de desenvolvedor que avaliamos é para desenvolvimento e prototipagem.

full_paragraphs: Researchers planted 2 million digital tripwires in requests sent through a sprawling network of AI services to find out what happened to sensitive information entrusted to them. What they discovered was an ecosystem that leaked highly sensitive data like a sieve.

The exposure was found through an ingenious experiment designed to test if sensitive information can leak through the vast chain of widely used AI services and how that information is exploited when it does. Many of today’s AI apps use services such as OpenRouter or Vercel that act as brokers. These “AI routers,” sometimes also known as “AI gateways,” receive large numbers of prompts sent from AI app end users and route them to an available inference engine based on criteria such as the one charging the lowest price or being best suited for the given task. Instead of using Anthropic, OpenAI, or another big provider, the developer hires an AI router to find the most suitable model.

Update, Nov 21: Posts on both Hacker News and X report that OpenRouter has sent customers an email notifying them that some of their prompts may have been read. OpenRouter cited the research and said that it received a report that the potential exposure involved prompts sent to MiniMax, a China-based model provider. OpenRouter said the researchers' planted URLs were accessed whether the prompts were sent to MiniMax directly or through three other resellers: AtlasCloud, Novita, and StreamLake. OpenRouter has removed a "Zero Data Retention" label from MiniMax-model endpoints. Hat tip: Sulat.com.

A exposição foi descoberta através de uma experiência engenhosa concebida para testar se informações sensíveis podem vazar através da vasta cadeia de serviços de IA amplamente utilizados e como essas informações são exploradas quando isso acontece. Muitos dos aplicativos de IA atuais usam serviços como OpenRouter ou Vercel que atuam como corretores. Esses “roteadores de IA”, às vezes também conhecidos como “gateways de IA”, recebem um grande número de prompts enviados de usuários finais de aplicativos de IA e os encaminham para um mecanismo de inferência disponível com base em critérios como aquele que cobra o preço mais baixo ou é o mais adequado para a tarefa determinada. Em vez de usar Anthropic, OpenAI ou outro grande fornecedor, o desenvolvedor contrata um roteador AI para encontrar o modelo mais adequado.

Para testar possíveis vazamentos, o pesquisador HD Moore reuniu uma coleção de chaves de acesso da Amazon Web Services, credenciais funcionais vinculadas a contas vazias da AWS, senhas para serviços como SSH e URLs exclusivos, nomes DNS e referências de repositórios git privados. Nenhum dos segredos havia sido usado antes e ele controlava a infraestrutura que recebia quaisquer solicitações usando as credenciais. Ele então semeou cada segredo em exatamente um prompt enviado a um único provedor. Caso algum dos segredos fosse divulgado, estes “canários” – assim chamados porque se assemelham ao papel daquela ave quando levado para as minas de carvão – permitiriam a Moore identificar cada elo da cadeia responsável.

items.title: The most misunderstood graph in AI just got a major update
items.summary: A new report from the AI evaluation nonprofit METR finds that some AI capabilities are continuing to improve along an exponential trajectory—but it also indicates that models aren’t quite as good at tasks that require judgment as they are at coding. The report is an update to the organization’s time horizon plot, which was widely…
full_paragraphs: A new report from the AI evaluation nonprofit METR finds that some AI capabilities are continuing to improve along an exponential trajectory—but it also indicates that models aren’t quite as good at tasks that require judgment as they are at coding.

The report is an update to the organization’s time horizon plot, which was widely shared— and widely misinterpreted, owing to the complexity of the measures it used. METR evaluated models by having them attempt a large suite of tasks, each of which had also been completed by humans. Each task’s difficulty was scored by how long it took the human testers to finish it—and then models were rated according to the length of the tasks that they could complete. That plot showed that AI systems were rapidly improving—every four months, the length of the tasks that frontier models could successfully complete doubled.

The updated plot adds more tasks—some that are estimated to take humans far longer than those in the original suite, and others that are more open-ended. One of the biggest questions in AI right now is the extent to which progress on “verifiable” tasks—where it’s possible to check automatically whether an AI system has succeeded or failed—carry over into tasks on which success or failure is harder to measure. We know how to teach neural networks how to do verifiable tasks: Researchers have the systems attempt one many times, strengthen the neural pathways that contribute to success, and weaken the pathways that contribute to failures. That’s why AI systems have become so good at coding and math, two domains where it’s possible to determine automatically whether a solution does or doesn’t work.

It’s much harder to apply this technique, known as reinforcement learning, to tasks where success is less well defined or takes longer to ascertain—such as choosing a new research direction. For the same reason, it’s tough to evaluate AI performance on these tasks, so METR’s original time horizon plot didn’t include any of them. But it’s precisely this type of task that will prove essential if AI systems are to automate research and development.

And AI research and development is an especially hot topic right now. Parts of the AI community are still reeling from a different, heavily redacted METR report from earlier this month, which claimed that AI might be speeding up the pace of AI progress at Anthropic by a factor of two. That report sparked fears that the company (which just had a blockbuster IPO) could soon achieve full recursive self-improvement, a regime in which AI systems autonomously design their own successors with no human involvement.

METR researchers have worked to make sure their new suite of tasks includes some of the fuzzier, judgment-laden ones that could be most relevant to AI research and development. In one task, they ask models to design new AI evaluations that METR could use in its research and then have human METR employees score the results. Even though the most advanced models are now better than almost every human at software engineering, here they fall short: Not one of the AI-designed evaluations was good enough for METR employees to consider it useful for their research.

In another task, models have to score philosophical arguments. This task is intended to capture the extent to which models can exercise good judgment—though METR writes in the report that employees disagree about how relevant the task is for automation of AI R&D. On this task, too, models fell short of human performance.

Though it’s difficult to score these new tasks—and even harder to determine what the scores mean—experts I spoke with appreciate that METR is incorporating new types of evaluations into its work. “We’re at the point where AI evaluations need to get more creative,” says Sayash Kapoor, a computer scientist and incoming professor at UC Berkeley. “Trying to push the envelope of the space of evaluations is a welcome change.”

full_paragraphs_pt: Um novo relatório da organização sem fins lucrativos de avaliação de IA METR conclui que algumas capacidades de IA continuam a melhorar ao longo de uma trajetória exponencial – mas também indica que os modelos não são tão bons em tarefas que exigem julgamento como são na codificação.

O relatório é uma atualização do gráfico do horizonte temporal da organização, que foi amplamente partilhado – e amplamente mal interpretado, devido à complexidade das medidas utilizadas. O METR avaliou os modelos fazendo-os tentar um grande conjunto de tarefas, cada uma das quais também concluída por humanos. A dificuldade de cada tarefa foi pontuada de acordo com o tempo que os testadores humanos levaram para concluí-la – e então os modelos foram classificados de acordo com a duração das tarefas que conseguiram concluir. Esse gráfico mostrou que os sistemas de IA estavam a melhorar rapidamente – a cada quatro meses, a duração das tarefas que os modelos de fronteira conseguiam completar com sucesso duplicava.

O enredo atualizado adiciona mais tarefas – algumas que estimam que levam muito mais tempo para os humanos do que aquelas do conjunto original e outras que são mais abertas. Uma das maiores questões da IA ​​neste momento é até que ponto o progresso em tarefas “verificáveis” – onde é possível verificar automaticamente se um sistema de IA foi bem-sucedido ou falhou – é transferido para tarefas nas quais o sucesso ou o fracasso são mais difíceis de medir. Sabemos como ensinar as redes neurais a realizar tarefas verificáveis: os pesquisadores fazem com que os sistemas tentem uma tarefa muitas vezes, fortalecendo os caminhos neurais que contribuem para o sucesso e enfraquecendo os caminhos que contribuem para o fracasso. É por isso que os sistemas de IA se tornaram tão bons em codificação e matemática, dois domínios onde é possível determinar automaticamente se uma solução funciona ou não.

É muito mais difícil aplicar esta técnica, conhecida como aprendizagem por reforço, a tarefas onde o sucesso é menos bem definido ou demora mais tempo a ser determinado – como a escolha de uma nova direção de investigação. Pela mesma razão, é difícil avaliar o desempenho da IA ​​nessas tarefas, então o gráfico de horizonte de tempo original do METR não incluía nenhuma delas. Mas é precisamente este tipo de tarefa que se revelará essencial para que os sistemas de IA possam automatizar a investigação e o desenvolvimento.

E a pesquisa e o desenvolvimento de IA são um tema especialmente importante no momento. Partes da comunidade de IA ainda estão se recuperando de um relatório METR diferente e fortemente redigido do início deste mês, que afirmava que a IA poderia estar acelerando o ritmo do progresso da IA ​​na Antrópica por um fator de dois. Esse relatório despertou receios de que a empresa (que acaba de realizar uma IPO de grande sucesso) possa em breve alcançar o auto-aperfeiçoamento recursivo completo, um regime em que os sistemas de IA concebem autonomamente os seus próprios sucessores, sem envolvimento humano.

Os pesquisadores do METR têm trabalhado para garantir que seu novo conjunto de tarefas inclua algumas das tarefas mais confusas e carregadas de julgamento que poderiam ser mais relevantes para a pesquisa e desenvolvimento de IA. Em uma tarefa, eles pedem aos modelos que projetem novas avaliações de IA que o METR possa usar em suas pesquisas e, em seguida, fazem com que funcionários humanos do METR classifiquem os resultados. Embora os modelos mais avançados sejam agora melhores do que quase todos os seres humanos em engenharia de software, aqui eles ficam aquém: nenhuma das avaliações concebidas pela IA foi suficientemente boa para que os funcionários do METR a considerassem útil para a sua investigação.

Numa outra tarefa, os modelos têm de pontuar argumentos filosóficos. Esta tarefa destina-se a captar até que ponto os modelos podem exercer o bom senso – embora o METR escreva no relatório que os funcionários discordam sobre a relevância da tarefa para a automação da I&D de IA. Também nesta tarefa os modelos ficaram aquém do desempenho humano.

Embora seja difícil pontuar estas novas tarefas – e ainda mais difícil determinar o significado das pontuações – os especialistas com quem falei apreciam o facto de o METR estar a incorporar novos tipos de avaliações no seu trabalho. “Estamos no ponto em que as avaliações de IA precisam ser mais criativas”, diz Sayash Kapoor, cientista da computação e professor iniciante na UC Berkeley. “Tentar ampliar o espaço das avaliações é uma mudança bem-vinda.”

full_paragraphs: A Russian national has been indicted on suspicions he was a Russian spy who stalked and surveilled employees of a Silicon Valley company that was assisting Ukraine in its ongoing war with its eastern neighbor.

Igor D’iu, 25, allegedly photographed the employees and their computer screens as they worked at a coffee shop located near the company’s Palo Alto office, federal prosecutors said Wednesday. He also kept a list of home addresses of employees and a senior executive. At one point, prosecutors said, D’iu trailed an employee as she traveled home from Palo Alto to San Francisco. An affidavit filed in the case referred to the employee as FEMP1, short for female employee, and said the event left her “in a state of emotional distress.”

“FEMP1 made evasive and irregular turns, took back roads, and turned into a grocery store parking lot where D’IU continued aggressively following her vehicle,” an FBI special agent wrote. “D’IU followed FEMP1 through U-turns, illegal left turns, and ran a red light to stay with FEMP1 for nearly thirty miles. FEMP1 called 911 while driving and was instructed to drive directly to San Francisco Police Department (“SFPD”) Mission Station. Near SFPD Mission Station, FEMP1 flagged an SFPD patrol vehicle and reported the incident. D’IU left once FEMP1 made contact with the patrol vehicle.”

items.title: NVIDIA and Microsoft Expand Accelerated Computing From Azure to Windows PCs
items.summary: NVIDIA and Microsoft are extending their full-stack collaboration to help organizations build, customize and deploy intelligent applications — from next-generation infrastructure on Azure to industrial systems and Windows PCs. At Microsoft Ignite, the companies are expanding access to Azure virtual machines powered by NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 systems, as well as adding customer availability to […]
full_paragraphs: NVIDIA and Microsoft are extending their full-stack collaboration to help organizations build, customize and deploy intelligent applications — from next-generation infrastructure on Azure to industrial systems and Windows PCs.

At Microsoft Ignite, the companies are expanding access to Azure virtual machines powered by NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 systems, as well as adding customer availability to NVIDIA open models and customization capabilities through Microsoft Foundry, and new options for running AI at the edge, where businesses generate and use their data.

Microsoft is also using NVIDIA technologies to accelerate its own models and services, including NVIDIA Dynamo inference software for post-training and NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs for Bing search models.
NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 systems are running in Azure data centers, providing infrastructure designed for demanding reasoning, agentic applications, and large-scale model training and inference.

Microsoft and NVIDIA are also collaborating to extend confidential computing to bare-metal and rack-scale AI infrastructure. The work will help protect sensitive models and data while they are being processed, supporting organizations that need to work with proprietary or regulated information.

NVIDIA Confidential Computing and attestation help customers verify the computing environment before releasing sensitive models, data or keys. As AI workloads span more interconnected accelerators, the companies are working to extend those protections across the AI factory infrastructure.
To help data centers get more performance from available power, NVIDIA and Microsoft are also collaborating on power efficiency using NVIDIA MaxLPS.

Azure’s Vera Rubin preview builds on NVIDIA and Microsoft’s codesign and performance optimization, underscored in the latest NVIDIA Blackwell-based MLPerf results. In MLPerf Training v6.1, Azure scaled to 10,240 NVIDIA GPUs with GB200 NVL72 systems on the DeepSeek-V3 model, the largest scale in the round. In MLPerf Inference v6.1, Azure’s NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 systems led cloud submissions on DeepSeek-R1 interactive throughput by over 10%, per Signal65.

full_paragraphs_pt: A NVIDIA e a Microsoft estão ampliando sua colaboração full-stack para ajudar as organizações a construir, personalizar e implantar aplicativos inteligentes — desde infraestrutura de próxima geração no Azure até sistemas industriais e PCs com Windows.

No Microsoft Ignite, as empresas estão expandindo o acesso às máquinas virtuais Azure alimentadas pelos sistemas NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72, bem como adicionando a disponibilidade do cliente aos modelos abertos e capacidades de personalização da NVIDIA através do Microsoft Foundry, e novas opções para executar IA na borda, onde as empresas geram e usam seus dados.

A Microsoft também está usando tecnologias NVIDIA para acelerar seus próprios modelos e serviços, incluindo software de inferência NVIDIA Dynamo para pós-treinamento e GPUs NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell para modelos de pesquisa do Bing.

Os sistemas NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 estão em execução em data centers do Azure, fornecendo infraestrutura projetada para raciocínio exigente, aplicativos de agente e treinamento e inferência de modelos em grande escala.

A Microsoft e a NVIDIA também estão colaborando para estender a computação confidencial à infraestrutura de IA bare-metal e em escala de rack. O trabalho ajudará a proteger modelos e dados confidenciais enquanto estão sendo processados, apoiando organizações que precisam trabalhar com informações proprietárias ou regulamentadas.

A computação confidencial e o atestado da NVIDIA ajudam os clientes a verificar o ambiente de computação antes de liberar modelos, dados ou chaves confidenciais. À medida que as cargas de trabalho de IA abrangem mais aceleradores interconectados, as empresas estão trabalhando para estender essas proteções a toda a infraestrutura da fábrica de IA.
Para ajudar os data centers a obterem mais desempenho com a energia disponível, a NVIDIA e a Microsoft também estão colaborando na eficiência energética usando NVIDIA MaxLPS.

A visualização do Vera Rubin do Azure baseia-se no codesign e na otimização de desempenho da NVIDIA e da Microsoft, ressaltados nos resultados mais recentes do MLPerf baseado em NVIDIA Blackwell. No MLPerf Training v6.1, o Azure foi dimensionado para 10.240 GPUs NVIDIA com sistemas GB200 NVL72 no modelo DeepSeek-V3, a maior escala da rodada. No MLPerf Inference v6.1, os sistemas NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 do Azure lideraram os envios em nuvem na taxa de transferência interativa DeepSeek-R1 em mais de 10%, de acordo com Signal65.

Developers are combining frontier AI models with NVIDIA Omniverse libraries to help carry out that work — building applications for exploring scenarios, investigating failures and improving designs.
Developers direct AI agents through natural-language instructions, review results and guide changes. Omniverse libraries provide GPU-accelerated physics, rendering and sensor simulation capabilities.
